claim: Saving surge 2021-24 is concentrated where mobile money grew (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d_sav~d_mm + terciles
effect: r=0.719 (n=58); terciles low/mid/high = +2.2/+11.6/+14.8pp
note: corr sample = 58 countries with MM data in both waves

claim: Resilience change 2021-24 aligns with mobile-money growth (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d_res~d_mm + terciles
gates: G3 ok, G4 ok, G6 FAIL (0.19 -> -0.005 after drop-top-5)
note: association is a big-country artifact; meaningful negative: MM moved saving (E1) but not resilience

claim: Gender-gap closure 2021-24 aligns with mobile-money growth (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d_gap~d_mm + terciles
effect: r=0.008 (n=59); terciles all ~+0.1pp; d_gap std 7.4pp but orthogonal to MM
note: clean null, verified against join bugs; gap changes are large but MM-unrelated in this window

claim: High usage-intensity 2021 leads account growth 2021-24 (dev panel)
test: weighted corr g20/account ratio vs d_account
effect: r=-0.590 (n=77) — OPPOSITE sign; terciles low/mid/high = +10.2/+2.1/+1.4pp
note: pre-registered direction rejected; reverse (catch-up) is strong but needs acc-level control -> E5b

claim: Accounts-first pattern: lower 2021 usage-intensity predicts faster 2021-24 account growth at same account level (dev panel)
test: weighted partial corr (ratio vs d_acc | acc21), WLS residualization
effect: r_partial=-0.595 (n=77) vs convergence benchmark -0.301
gates: G4 ok (77c, 100%), G6 sign-stable but magnitude drops to -0.114 w/o top-5
note: CAVEAT: effect concentrated in large economies; descriptive, not causal

claim: Where formal saving surged, savings became a bigger emergency-funds source (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d(fin24sav)~d(saved_formally) 2021-24
effect: r=0.541 (n=76); dev aggregate fin24sav 17.9->20.3pp
gates: G3 declared (fin24sav), G4 ok (76c, 97.4%), G6 sign-stable (0.54->0.24)
note: links E1+E2: saving surge shifts resilience composition before headline resilience moves

claim: Dormancy J-curve: bigger 2014-17 account drives -> higher 2017 inactivity (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d_acc(14-17)~inactivity-ratio(17)
effect: r=0.825 (n=77) BUT collapses to 0.014 w/o top-5
gates: G4 ok; G6 sign-check passes mechanically but magnitude collapse = one-country-story per gate intent
note: true as population-weighted statement (India-dominated), not as cross-country regularity; gate-design lesson logged

claim: Income-gap re-widening 2021-24 proportional to poorest-40 jump 2017-21 (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d_poor40(17-21)~d_gap(21-24)
gates: G4 ok, G6 n/a at this magnitude
note: clean null: no systematic reversion of the 2021 narrowing

claim: Not enough money (fin11a) barrier among unbanked adults is an income-graded reason, most cited by the poorest (2024 wave)
test: weighted rate of fin11a==1 among account==0, by inc_q
gates: M2 ok (n 3352-4894 per quintile, all >>100)
note: single 2024 cross-section, descriptive only; calibration pre-check (not the formal result) picked fin11a as income-sensitive vs fin11b-f

claim: Mobile-only accountholders are younger and less educated than bank-only accountholders (2024 wave)
test: weighted share aged<=35 and share primary-educ-only, mobile-only vs bank-only
effect: young<=35: 65.4pp vs 40.6pp (diff 24.7pp); primary_only: 47.8pp vs 41.1pp (diff 6.7pp)
gates: M2 ok (n=10340 mobile-only, n=24037 bank-only)
note: single 2024 cross-section, descriptive only; consistent with mobile money as on-ramp for underbanked/younger populations

claim: Money-barrier prevalence (fin11a, 2024) predicts slower 2021-24 account growth (dev panel)
test: weighted corr fin11a_2024 vs d_account(21-24)
effect: r=-0.263 (n=47); below |r|>=0.30 threshold
gates: G3 n/a (fin11a has no variant choice), G4 ok (47c, 59.7% pop), G6 ok sign-stable+magnitude-retaining (-0.263 -> -0.255)
note: direction as hypothesized (more constrained -> slower growth) and gates clean, but effect below keep threshold; a weak, gate-clean null

claim: Gender gap in account ownership is wider among the poorest income quintile than the richest (2024 wave, pooled)
test: weighted account rate by female x inc_q; gap=male-female for q1 vs q5
effect: gap_q1=5.2pp, gap_q5=5.7pp, diff=-0.5pp (opposite of hypothesized direction, negligible)
gates: M2 ok (n 10478-19120 per cell)
note: clean null; gender gap in account ownership is essentially flat across income quintile in this pooled cross-section (fixed a female-coding bug in first run attempt: raw coding is 1=female/2=male, not 0/1 -- caught before any result was read)

claim: G2P payment digitalization (2021) predicts subsequent account growth (dev panel)
test: weighted corr fing2p_acc_2021 vs d_account(21-24)
effect: r=-0.410 (n=77) — OPPOSITE sign from hypothesized
gates: G3 n/a (fing2p_acc has no variant choice), G4 ok (77c, 100%), G6 ok sign-stable+magnitude-retaining (-0.410 -> -0.483)
note: direction rejected like E5; reads as convergence (less G2P-account penetration = more room to grow), not a causal on-ramp effect; no E5b-style follow-up spawned this cycle (budget)

claim: Digital payment adoption (anydigpayment) is lower among 65+ adults than prime-working-age adults (2024 wave, pooled)
test: weighted rate of anydigpayment by age band (15-25/26-35/36-50/51-65/65+)
effect: 36-50=56.8pp vs 65+=48.1pp; diff=8.7pp; full shape 45.0/59.7/56.8/53.5/48.1pp (inverted-U, peak at 26-35)
gates: M2 ok (n=10216-26551 per band, all >>100)
note: single 2024 cross-section, descriptive only; peak band (26-35) younger than pre-registered comparison band (36-50), but pre-registered 36-50-vs-65+ diff still clears threshold

claim: The 2021-24 formal-saving surge co-moves with wage digitalization (d fin32_acc) as strongly as with mobile money E1 (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d(fin32_acc)~d(fin17a_17a1_d) 2021-24 + terciles
effect: r=0.791 (n=71); terciles low/mid/high = +3.2/+10.9/+13.6pp
gates: G3 n/a (fin32_acc no variant), G4 ok (71c, 68.6% pop), G6 ok sign+magnitude-retaining (0.791->0.785)
note: descriptive; account growth a plausible common driver; broad-based digitalization channel parallel to E1's MM channel; big-economy caveat but jackknife barely moves

claim: 'Family member already has an account' barrier (fin11f) among unbanked is cited more by women than men (2024, pooled)
test: weighted rate of fin11f==1 among account==0, split by female (1=F/2=M)
effect: women=24.8pp vs men=27.9pp; diff=-3.1pp (opposite direction, below 5pp threshold)
gates: M2 ok (n=13026 women / 7863 men, both >>100); M3 n/a (no country-file equivalent)
note: clean null; slightly reversed and below threshold; classic 'women mediated through household account' pattern absent in pooled economy-equal 2024 cross-section (may be region-specific; caveat #3)

claim: Formal borrowing and formal saving deepen together 2021-24 (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d(fin22a_22a1_22g_d)~d(fin17a_17a1_d) 2021-24 + terciles
effect: r=0.403 (n=76); d_borrow terciles low/mid/high mean d_saving = +5.8/+17.2/+13.4pp
gates: G3 ok (both headlines), G4 ok (76c, 97.4%), G6 ok sign+magnitude-retaining (0.403->0.471)
note: descriptive; broad balance-sheet deepening, not saving-specific; account growth/income shocks plausible common drivers (noted, not controlled); tercile shape non-monotonic (mid>high) but corr+gates clean

claim: Formal saving (fin17a) is strongly education-graded; least-educated barely reached (2024, pooled)
test: weighted rate of fin17a==1 by educ (1=primary-/2=secondary/3=tertiary), all adults
effect: tertiary=46.2pp vs primary=12.0pp; diff=+34.1pp (monotonic 12.0/22.6/46.2)
gates: M2 ok (n=35073/53354/14103, all >>100); M3 n/a (fin17a-only, no exact country equiv; subgroup split)
note: single 2024 cross-section, descriptive only; formal-saving depth margin far less reached among primary-educ adults; complements M1's income gradient on the access barrier

claim: Digital-payment adoption growth co-moves with the formal-saving surge 2021-24 (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d(g20_any)~d(fin17a_17a1_d) 2021-24 + terciles
effect: r=0.370 (n=76); d_g20 terciles low/mid/high mean d_saving = +2.8/+16.7/+14.4pp
gates: G3 ok (both headlines), G4 ok (76c, 97.4%), G6 ok sign+magnitude-retaining (0.370->0.782, jackknife grows)
note: descriptive; adds digital-payment usage to E1(MM)/E10(wages)/E11(borrowing) as a 4th broad-digitalization channel of the surge; account growth plausible common driver (noted, not controlled); tercile shape concave (mid>high) but corr+gates clean

claim: 'Too far away' barrier (fin11b) among unbanked is cited more by rural than urban adults (2024, pooled)
test: weighted rate of fin11b==1 among account==0, split by urbanicity (1=rural/2=urban)
effect: rural=36.0pp vs urban=36.8pp; diff=-0.8pp (opposite direction, far below 5pp threshold)
gates: M2 ok (n=12992 rural / 7859 urban, both >>100); M3 n/a (no country-file equivalent)
note: clean null; the physical-distance barrier is cited at near-identical rates by rural and urban unbanked in the pooled economy-equal 2024 cross-section (within-country rural/urban gaps may wash out under pooling; caveat #3)

claim: FI-account and mobile-money account growth are complements (co-development), not substitutes (leapfrogging), 2021-24 (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d(fiaccount_t_d)~d(mobileaccount_t_d) 2021-24 + terciles
effect: r=0.435 (n=59); d_fi terciles low/mid/high mean d_mm = -2.8/+14.6/+12.3pp
gates: G3 ok (both headlines), G4 ok (62c, 71.3% pop), G6 ok sign+magnitude-retaining (0.435->0.347, above 0.5x floor 0.218)
note: descriptive; positive co-movement supports broad-digitalization/co-development reading over substitution/leapfrogging; big-economy caveat but jackknife retains magnitude; tercile shape concave (mid>high)

claim: Usage-side gender gap conditional on access: anydigpayment lower among women than men among accountholders (2024, pooled)
test: weighted rate of anydigpayment among account==1, split by female (1=F/2=M)
effect: men=86.8pp vs women=83.4pp; diff=+3.4pp (right direction but below 5pp threshold)
gates: M2 ok (n=34249 women / 32882 men, both >>100); M3 n/a (within-accountholder split, no country equiv)
note: gate-clean, right direction, below threshold; conditional on holding an account the usage-side gender gap is small (3.4pp), much smaller than access-margin gaps; descriptive single 2024 cross-section

claim: Digitalization on-ramps are bundled: mobile-money and digital-payment usage grow together 2021-24 (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d(mobileaccount_t_d)~d(g20_any) 2021-24 + terciles
effect: r=0.600 (n=58); d_mm terciles low/mid/high mean d_g20 = -6.0/+10.4/+9.7pp
gates: G3 ok (both headlines), G4 ok (76c, 97.4% pop), G6 ok sign+magnitude-retaining (0.600->0.775, jackknife grows)
note: descriptive; Delta(mobile-money) & Delta(g20) themselves strongly co-move, so E1/E12's separate 'channels' are one bundled digitalization phenomenon across access & usage margins; account growth plausible common driver (noted, not controlled); tercile shape concave (mid>high)

claim: Account ownership (access margin) is strongly education-graded; even wider in pp than U4's formal-saving depth gradient (2024, pooled)
test: weighted rate of account==1 by educ (1=primary-/2=secondary/3=tertiary), all adults
effect: tertiary=93.4pp vs primary=51.9pp; diff=+41.5pp (monotonic 51.9/77.7/93.4)
gates: M2 ok (n=38398/74624/30480, all >>100); M3 n/a (within-educ subgroup split, no exact country equiv)
note: single 2024 cross-section, descriptive only; education stratifies access even more (41.5pp) than depth (U4 formal-saving 34.1pp) in absolute pp -- the pre-registered 'less sharply' secondary guess was wrong (bases differ: account 52-93pp vs saving 12-46pp), but the >=5pp keep condition holds; complements U4/M1

claim: Resilience change 2021-24 tracks the formal-saving surge where it landed (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d(fin24aSD_ND)~d(fin17a_17a1_d) 2021-24 + terciles
effect: r=0.031 (n=76); d_sav terciles low/mid/high mean d_res = -3.0/+3.9/+0.7pp (non-monotonic)
gates: G3 ok (both headlines), G4 ok (76c, 97.4%), G6 mechanically ok (0.031->0.133) but moot at this magnitude
note: clean informative null: even where saving surged most, resilience did not move within 3 years; with E2 (d_res orthogonal to d_mm) and E7 (emergency-fund composition shifted) the story sharpens to a saving-vs-resilience gap; descriptive, window may be too short for stock accumulation

claim: Depth-side gender gap conditional on access: formal saving (fin17a) lower among women than men among accountholders (2024, pooled)
test: weighted rate of fin17a==1 among account==1, split by female (1=F/2=M)
effect: men=34.5pp vs women=29.5pp; unrounded diff=+4.96pp (right direction, just below 5pp threshold)
gates: M2 ok (n=34249 women / 32882 men, both >>100); M3 n/a (within-accountholder split, no country equiv)
note: borderline discard by the pre-registered threshold (4.955<5); depth-side conditional gap larger than U6's usage-side 3.4pp but still small vs access-margin gradients (U4/U7 34-42pp); conditional-on-access gender gaps are consistently small; descriptive single 2024 cross-section

claim: Account-ownership growth co-moves with the formal-saving surge 2021-24 (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d(account_t_d)~d(fin17a_17a1_d) 2021-24 + terciles
effect: r=0.198 (n=76); below 0.30 threshold; d_account terciles low/mid/high mean d_saving = +15.4/+9.6/+14.3pp (non-monotonic)
gates: G3 ok (both headlines), G4 ok (77c, 100%), G6 sign-stable and jackknife GROWS (0.198->0.741 drop-top-5)
note: informative discard: the pop-weighted account~saving co-movement is weak because the largest economies (most account growth) are where formal saving surged LEAST — drop them and r jumps to 0.741; the saving surge is a depth phenomenon not reducible to raw account expansion, partly relieving the standing 'account growth common driver' caveat on E1/E10-E14; descriptive

claim: Documentation barrier (fin11d) among unbanked is education-graded; least-educated cite it most (2024, pooled)
test: weighted rate of fin11d==1 among account==0, by educ (1=primary-/2=secondary/3=tertiary)
effect: primary=54.2pp vs tertiary=46.0pp; diff=+8.2pp (monotonic 54.2/48.6/46.0)
gates: M2 ok (n=9714/9995/1086, all >>100); M3 n/a (barrier-among-unbanked split, no country equiv)
note: single 2024 cross-section, descriptive only; documentation barrier has a high base rate (~half of unbanked cite it) and education grades it modestly (+8.2pp), the natural stratifier for a formal-paperwork barrier; complements M1 (income grades money barrier +10.3pp) vs U3/U5 barrier nulls

claim: Formal-saving surge 2021-24 is a catch-up phenomenon (lower 2021 level -> larger gain, dev panel)
test: weighted corr saving_2021 level ~ d(fin17a_17a1_d) 2021-24 + terciles; account_t_d same test as benchmark
effect: r=+0.480 (n=76) — OPPOSITE sign (divergence, not catch-up); 2021-level terciles low/mid/high mean change = +8.5/+13.0/+15.8pp; account benchmark r=-0.301 (n=77)
gates: G3 ok (both headlines), G4 ok (76c, 97.4%), G6 FAIL for saving (0.480 -> -0.135 drop-top-5, retention -0.281); account benchmark G6 ok (-0.301 -> -0.457)
note: double rejection: pre-registered catch-up direction rejected, and the observed opposite (divergence — saving deepened fastest where it was already deepest) is a big-country artifact that flips sign without the top-5, so no general claim either way; the account benchmark DOES show gate-clean catch-up (r=-0.301, jackknife grows), so access and depth margins behave oppositely on level-vs-change — access converges, depth does not; declared regression-to-mean confound applies to both equally and cannot explain a positive saving r

claim: Conditional on holding an account, digital-payment usage is strongly education-graded (2024, pooled)
test: weighted rate of anydigpayment==1 among account==1, by educ (1=primary-/2=secondary/3=tertiary)
effect: tertiary=94.1pp vs primary=77.3pp; diff=+16.8pp (monotonic 77.3/87.7/94.1); unconditional context 37.3/60.4/84.0 (gap 46.7pp)
gates: M2 ok (n=17067/37350/12478, all >>100); M3 n/a (within-accountholder split, no country equiv)
note: single 2024 cross-section, descriptive only; answers the open question left by U6/U8 — 'conditional on access, gaps are small' is specific to GENDER (3.4pp/4.96pp), not general: education still grades usage by 16.8pp among accountholders, though access does most of the sorting (unconditional gap 46.7pp shrinks to 16.8pp, ~64% absorbed); complements U4/U7

claim: The formal-saving surge 2021-24 displaced borrowing as an emergency-funds source (dev panel)
test: weighted corr d(fin24bor)~d(fin17a_17a1_d) 2021-24 + terciles; other sources reported descriptively
effect: r=+0.069 (n=76) — near-zero and WRONG sign (borrowing did not recede); d_sav terciles low/mid/high mean d_bor = +1.0/-0.3/+4.0pp (high tercile borrowing rose); descriptive context: d_sell r=-0.372 (ret 0.41), d_work r=-0.489 (ret 0.28), d_fam r=+0.067
gates: G3 declared n/a (fin24bor composition indicator, no variant; fin17a headline ok), G4 ok (76c, 97.4%), G6 FAIL for borrow (0.069->-0.021)
note: clean informative null: borrowing was NOT the displaced source where saving surged (mirror of E7 which found savings became a BIGGER source r=0.541); descriptively the co-declining sources were selling assets and extra work, not borrowing, but neither survives G6 magnitude-retention (0.41/0.28<0.5) so no general claim; compositional-complementarity caveat declared; descriptive

claim: Mobile-only accountholders are drawn more from the poorest two income quintiles than bank-only (2024, pooled)
test: weighted share inc_q in {1,2} among mobile-only (account_mob==1 & account_fin==0) vs bank-only (account_fin==1 & account_mob==0)
effect: mobile-only=33.8pp vs bank-only=38.8pp; diff=-5.0pp (OPPOSITE direction — mobile-only slightly LESS poor); quintile profile mobile-only q1-q5=15/19/22/22/20 vs bank-only 19/20/20/20/20
gates: M2 ok (n=10340 mobile-only / 24037 bank-only, both >>100); M3 n/a (within-accountholder composition split, no country equiv)
note: informative discard: M2 s "mobile money as on-ramp for the underserved" holds on AGE and EDUCATION but NOT income — mobile-only accountholders skew young and less-educated yet are marginally less poor than bank-only; caveat: inc_q is within-economy relative quintile, economy-equal pooling mixes economies (caveat #3); descriptive single 2024 cross-section
